relations: Fingers touching outer dome sides causes deformation and leaning, while the central seam remains closed.
Contact with the right dome breaks its smooth film into a billowing vapor cloud.
The left dome's film remains coherent but deformed, and liquid levels stay unchanged.
caption: The video captures two stemmed glasses side by side, each holding dark red liquid beneath a large iridescent dome of white vapor. The domes touch along a vertical seam, and each surface reflects two rectangular lights. A person in a black apron and blue plaid shirt stands behind the glasses with hands resting at the lower edges, a ring visible on one hand. The domes remain rounded and intact while only small shifts appear in the reflected light patches. The resting hands then withdraw and return as two extended index fingers approaching from the sides. The fingers touch the outer sides of the left and right domes. As they touch, the domes deform and the tops lean, though the central seam stays closed. The right dome soon loses its smooth film and becomes a billowing white vapor cloud that spreads outward. The left dome remains a coherent but deformed film, while the red liquid levels in both glasses stay unchanged.
